incident_description: We had a string of grinch Christmas lights that we have hung by our tv. We were playing them and left them on the floor when we went to put our kids to bed. We came back 10 minutes later and the item was extremely hot and began to melt the plastic. We took the batteries out and it appeared to have started to expand the batteries as well. If not caught when we did, it would have caught on fire.
justification: The incident involved overheating and potential fire hazard, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
Hi. I would like to file a report about a chairs I purchased on Walmart.com in December. It was a 24" swivel chair. Last week I noticed my 19 month old daughter chewing on something. I checked and found a very small ball bearing. Come to find out it came from the chairs. I immediately put them away  in the garage to keep it away from my daughter.  Talking to Walmart customer service, I was told to call manufacturer  which is Cheyenne Products. Got their phone #, called, no answer. Next step is to report unsafe product.  Below link shows what king of chair it is. Please review and advise. 

https://www.walmart.com/ip/Mainstays-24-Ladder-Back-Barstool-Multiple-Colors/49933656

Thank You for Your time. 
[REDACTED]
justification: A small ball bearing came loose from the chair, posing a choking hazard to a child, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: i have an oxo scissors. This scissors come apart so you can clean it. However, i was holding the scissors and it came apart and it fell. It almost hit my daughter. This product should be recalled. scissor's edge is very sharp and it could've caused a serious damage if it fell on my daugher.
justification: The scissors came apart and fell, nearly hitting the daughter, but no injury occurred. The sharp edges pose a potential injury risk if it happens again.

incident_description: I sent a message to the company with no response. I was burning a bath & body works candle. It set off my smoke alarm so I blew out the candle when I went to check it I noticed the paper wrapper was burnt off
justification: The incident involved a candle causing minor damage (burnt wrapper) but no injury or further harm.

incident_description:
I purchased a floor lamp in Nov 2015.  I did not assemble and start using it until approximately end of Jan 2016.  I noticed after having it awhile it went thru light bulbs a lot faster than my previous floor lamps.  Over the past year it started blowing even more light bulbs. 
Today I had went to do laundry and came back and the light had turned off.  I assumed the bulb needed replaced so I went and got one.  When I put the bulb in and turned the switch it made an "electrifying noise" and burst at the same time.  Then I smelled burnt stuff.  I quickly unplugged the lamp.  
Upon removing light bulb I seen that it had blown an actual hole in the bottom of the bulb.  I then considered removing the cord and socket and just replacing the components.  Upon removing the top part of the socket I seen that it had even blown a hole thru the socket as well.  I do not feel as though this should have happened.  Had I not been home I feel as though it would have caught on fire.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning lamp that could have caused a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I am Assistant Attorney General. Recently, our Office conducted an investigation into the presence of lead and cadmium in childrens school supplies. Our investigation uncovered numerous childrens school supplies offered for sale and purchased by consumers contained levels of lead in excess of that permitted by the federal Consumer Product Safety Improvement Act.

justification: The presence of lead in children's school supplies poses a risk of injury due to lead exposure, but no specific injuries or deaths are mentioned.

incident_description:
(04/2017) The consumer stated that her daughter screamed that something was smoking. The consumer came into the room to check and saw that the shop light was smoking and popping. The smoke was coming from the end of the cord exit at the fixture. The consumer unplugged the product.

(05/30/2017) The consumer stated that the same thing happened again. The light started flickering for about 30 seconds. The light started smoking, then it popped. The consumer unplugged the product and took it outside. The consumer had contacted the fire department and was advised to leave the product outside so that it could cool off.
justification: The incident involved a smoking and popping shop light, posing a fire hazard but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: The light switch had previously been turned "on" but no one was in the (laundry) room. When entering the room I saw the fixture lying on the floor together with the bulb casing and fragments of the fixture. The casing surrounding the filament had fallen off, the filament was still screwed into the bulb socket and was lit.
justification: The incident involved a light fixture falling and breaking, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Ikea Malm glass top shattered for no reason. In the middle of the night I was woken to a large crashing/bang noise in the bedroom. I found the shattered glass top spread throughout the room. Nothing fell onto or caused the glass to shatter like it did.
justification: The glass shattered unexpectedly, causing a disturbance but no injury.

incident_description: Lithonia Emergency Lighting was recalled in 2014 as a potential fire hazard. The Burlington, VT Fire Marshal's Office did a safety inspection at a local business finding several emergency lights that did not work, and the Facilities Manager showed them samples of the recalled lighting that showed no signs of overheating several years ago but now show definite signs of overheating. The Facilities Manager said the firm had told him they would replace any panels that had turned brown from overheating near a potentially faulty resister, and the Facilities Manager worked with the firm to replace approximately 20 units out of a total of 42 in 2015. When the Facilities Manager began to replace the units with newer LED's, he found that many of the panels left unrepaired/ uncorrected in 2015 were now showing evidence of overheating. The Fire Marshal brought the concern to the CPSC's area representative who then contacted Headquarters. Compliance requested samples and an in-depth investigation report.
justification: The incident involves recalled emergency lighting showing signs of overheating, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths have been reported.

incident_description: After it was lit for about an hour the candle glass enclosure blew up and top piece broke off so. It also caused large flame that could have caused fire in my home. I was able to put it out quickly with minimal property damage.
justification: The incident involved property damage and a potential fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I have had a Cree 13.5 watt light bulb on my daughters night stand in a lamp for over a year.  I was reading her a book this evening and noticed the light was smoking.  Upon further inspection I realized the bottom of the bulb had caught fire.  This was of immediate concern and extreme worry to me.
justification: The bulb caught fire, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer noticed that the task light protective coating cracked at the transformer exposing the cooper wires. 

The firm was contacted and was advised that the 90 day warranty had a expired. However since she showed a great concern about their product they would be willing to mail a new light out. 

She is responsible to mail the facility light in and pay for the shipping for both hers and the new one.

The consumer estimates using the light for  12 days or more day for the almost two years that she has had it.
justification: The cracked protective coating exposes copper wires, posing a potential electrical hazard, but no injury or incident was reported.

incident_description:
My bathroom scale was a model made by the Taylor Precision Products company, they are located in Las Cruces, NM. We have owned this item for around one year having purchased it in the local K-Mart. It is model #7506 which had a glass top which was stood on to obtain your weight from a digital readout.

A few days ago when my wife stepped on the unit to get her weight it shattered with such force that shards of glass and small pieces of glass traveled at least 10-15 feet. Glass covered the bathroom and adjacent bedroom. She sustained glass cuts to her feet and legs, has tiny flakes of glass all over her body and one in her right eye. The scale was on the floor, had never been dropped or damaged in any way. My wife weighs approximately 140 pounds, I weigh approximately 190 lbs, neither of us have ever used the scale in any way other than to stand on it barefoot.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (cuts and glass flakes on the body and eye) but no death, warranting a severity level of 3. The likelihood is considered rare (1) as the scale shattered unexpectedly under normal use.

incident_description: Got a recall notice on our bed we purchased from Wayfair on 06/20/2020. The bed is sagging and going to break at this point.
justification: The bed is sagging and at risk of breaking, but no injury or incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: daylight Compact FLuorescent bulbs exploded in the car in the home driveway. 52 yof sustained knee laceration due to the explosion.
justification: The incident resulted in a knee laceration, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
3/24/14- The consumer stated that she had her 6 month old 17 pound son seated on the infant seat for 10 minutes. He was chewing on a piece of the restraint belt for 2 minutes. The consumer hears her son making gasping sounds. She noticed that he was choking on something. The consumer was able to retrieve the item from his throat after 60 seconds. After dislodging the item from his throat, she realizes that he was choking on the plastic thin warning label that was glued to the restraint belt of the seat. The consumer took her son to a pediatrician named [REDACTED]. He determined that the child was not injured and advised the consumer to observe the infant and return in the event of any seizure or abnormal behavior. The consumer discontinued the use of the infant seat.

3/25/14- The consumer contacted the manufacturer. She spoke with [REDACTED]. [REDACTED] offered a replacement. The consumer would have to send pictures of the seat and return the seat first in order to get a replacement. Otherwise, the consumer could "keep the seat and pretend this never happened".

This product is affected by recall #08-046 and was repaired according to the remedy.

The consumer thinks this product poses a choking and injury hazard to the infants.
justification: The infant choked on a warning label but was not injured, and the product was previously recalled and repaired.

incident_description: Went out for lunch at around 11:30am and return around 3pm to find the whole floor full of shattered glass everywhere.
justification: The description reports an incident with shattered glass but no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
The light is used over our stove and is left on 24 hours a day 7 days a week.  It has been in place for about 3 months.  It is never turned off.

On Wednesday afternoon it exploded.

Glass shards were scattered up to 4 feet away and glass fell all over our stove and kitchen counters.

There was no warning.  The light did not dim or make any noise.

There were no visible power fluctuations.  I was home at the time working on my computer and was within 20 feet of the light when it failed.
justification: The light exploded, scattering glass shards but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I am unsure when my bumbo seat was manufactured but I know it was before 2009. My seven month old daughter has fallen forward out of this seat as I do not have the seat belt attachment for it yet. I didn't even know it was under recall until today when I seen it on the news. My daughter only had minor bruising and was ok.

However, I think that people should be aware that the child (as my son and my daughter has both)been able to move the chair. I do not have carpeting; just hardwood floors and tile. Both children were able to use their feet to scoot backwards posing a risk to their safety if stairs, cords, etc are near by. I would hate to see that a child died or was seriously hurt by being able to scoot the chair around and nothing was ever said. I think that a warning should be noted about use on smooth surfaces.
justification: The child suffered minor bruising from falling out of the seat, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood of recurrence is likely (4) due to the described ability of children to move the chair on smooth surfaces.

incident_description: 4 mo old female infant placed to sleep on back in crib on Boppy Newborn Lounger, with bottle propped with blanket and a stuffed unicorn with arms at head of crib and lounger. Was found with head under unicorn pillow and blanket, prone and unresponsive.
justification: The infant was found unresponsive, indicating a severe outcome.

incident_description: Our first incident was our three year old daughter was sleeping and got he arm stuck between the mattress and bed frame. There is a gap between them. She was not seriously injured but her arm was red and swollen. It hurt her when we removed her arm from the bed. Our second problem is that the slats are not safe. My daughter weighs 30lbs and three slats cracked underneath her bed. We took the bunk beds down because we were scared. I feel this bunk bed set is very unsafe and should not have you and children using them. I wasted $200 dollars because I have to buy I new set because I will not let my children use them. They are poorly made and the wood cracks extremely easy.
justification: The daughter's arm was red and swollen, indicating an injury, and the slats cracked under her weight, showing a likely recurrence risk.

incident_description: My husband had our 5.5 month old son in his Bumbo.  He was seated on a level counter away from the edge.  My husband looked away briefly to start bath water and my son and the Bumbo crashed off the three foot counter.  My son had to go to the emergency for a bleeding mouth and nose.  Fortunately he only suffered a fat lip and a torn frenulum.  While the directions do say to only use the Bumbo on the floor I believe this warning is not strong enough.  We have used it many times in similar situations with multiple children and had no problem.  Perhaps there should be additional non skid material on the bottom to make it less likely to move across a surface.
justification: The incident resulted in a bleeding mouth and nose, requiring emergency care, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as similar situations have occurred without incident before, but the risk remains.

incident_description: An 87-M was sitting on a white plastic chair when a front leg broke causing him to fall and strike his head on the ground on 01/24/2014.  He did not lose consciousness and did not immediately seek medical attention.  The decedent began c/o headache and demonstrated decreased level of consciousness by the following day.  A head CT taken 1-2 days later revealed an intracranial bleed (subdural hematoma).
justification: The incident resulted in a subdural hematoma and death, indicating the highest severity level.

incident_description: On 6/12/23, shortly before [REDACTED] AM CT, my twelve year old came into my bedroom to report her bed burning. There I found her Beurer cozy-soft fleece throw smoking and burning through her bed and bedding. I used a fire extinguisher to quell the burning that had spread into the mattress my child was laying on while asleep. The overheat failsafe failed. Chunks of the blanket melted to my child resulting in second degree burns.
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns to the child, indicating an injury, and the failure of the overheat failsafe suggests a possible recurrence.

incident_description: Tree topper started on fire
justification: A tree topper catching fire is an incident with potential for injury or property damage, but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description: 83 year old female with history of diabetes and dementia.  Wheelchair bound and requires assistance into bed.  Was found wedged between the mattress and bed safety rail in her room with the bed rail pressed firmly against the right side of her neck.  Possible positional asphyxia.  The family mentioned that they purchased the item on Amazon.  The item was used by the decedent to help her get out of bed.
justification: The incident resulted in death due to positional asphyxia, and the use of the bed safety rail by a vulnerable individual increases the likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
Patio Swivel Chair Anselmo was being used during a luncheon. I fell as chair base broke. I received some scrapes, bruises and hit my head on the concrete patio.   I was not able to work on the following Monday because I hurt all over and had bruises. RI statue of limitations for personal injury is 3 years.   I am reporting this on  February 3 2017. 

We disposed  the chair. Now we have only 1. Now that we find out it was defective We Are asking for a chair replacement.
justification: The incident resulted in scrapes, bruises, and a head injury, and the person was unable to work the following day, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as the chair was defective but has now been disposed of.

incident_description: I received a notice today from Amazon to report a recall on an item I purchased for my mother, the Medline bed assist rail.  In August 2021, the rail malfunctioned and caused her to fall hard. She had to enter a nursing home where her condition continued to deteriorate. In May 2022, she began showing symptoms of sepsis. The physician determined that the fall was hard enough to cause the failure of a mesh sling installed after a hysterectomy to support her bladder. Over the months since the fall, her bladder had descended to her colon where a fistula formed that caused feces to enter her bladder. She died painfully a few days later.
justification: The malfunction of the bed assist rail led to a fall, severe complications, and ultimately death.

incident_description: My nearly three month old son was wearing a Dreamland Baby Co product, the Dream Weighted Sleep Swaddle. I laid him to sleep and when I left the room I was able to see his face. When I returned, he was face down. I believe he turn and couldn't turn back from the weight of the sleep sack. He passed away.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of the infant due to the inability to turn back from the weighted sleep swaddle.

incident_description: 4 and 1/2 month old female fraternal twin was swaddled with her twin, on a shared Twin Z pillow in their crib at 1330 hours.  When the decedent's mother returned to see them 35 minutes later, the decedent's head had slipped down between the pillow and fabric wall of the crib.  The back of her head was against the pillow and her face was against the fabric wall.  Bystander CPR was performed and she was transported to the ER where she was pronounced.  The crib's bed area was ten inches deep with a length of three feet and a width of two feet.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of the infant due to positional asphyxia, and the setup with shared swaddling in a confined crib space increases the likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Pendant Chandelier from Pottery barn kids purchased in 2017 collapsed in the middle of night in my twins room and shattered glass all over.
justification: The chandelier collapsed and shattered glass, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: 1 1/2 month old infant propped on boppy pillow for sleep.
justification: Propping an infant on a Boppy pillow for sleep increases the risk of suffocation or positional asphyxia, which can lead to death.

incident_description:
Baby was using a x-small zipadee zip transitional swaddle to sleep. She was wearing a diaper and a thin long sleeved shirt underneath. Baby is 9lbs 9oz and 22 inches long. So well within the limits for that size.. 
She was placed on her back asleep into her bassinett. Whenever she would raise her arms up next to her head the fabric from the chest area would come up and cover her mouth and nose entirely.   No injuries happened as I noticed before going to bed and was able to change products for sleep.  Im concerned this product may be a suffocation risk since even with correctly sized the fabric is able to come up and cover the face.
justification: No injuries occurred, but the product poses a suffocation risk as described.

incident_description: A loft bed by the name LuLu made by Ashley furniture was purchased from Slumberland furniture in Waite Park MN on 8/31/13. It was also delivered and assembled by Slumberland employees. The incident occurred February 26,2014 which led to the death of a four year old girl. The girl was playing in her room. She asked to watch a movie so her mother started the movie and left her in her room. The mother thought things were quiet but thought her daughter may have fallen asleep. A short while later the mother went to check on her to find her stuck in between the wall and her loft bed. The girls mother attempted CPR while on the phone with 911. The ambulance arrived and transported her to the Litchfield Hospital in MN. The girl died. Meeker County did an investigation to ensure no foul play and found it to be a terrible accident. After this incident occurred I examined the bed to see if there was any product flaws that could be noted. I did find that there is a shelving unit on one end that supported the bed frame that stuck out a little bit. After speaking with her mother she said that one time she had gone behind the bed and had her feet on top of the shelving unit for support. Her mother had to help her get out and told her daughter to never do that again because she might not be there to help her get unstuck. I don't know what happened the evening when she got stuck which led to her death but I believe she may have tried doing what she had done before but was to far over that her feet did not catch the shelving unit this time and she ended up being hung by the loft bed. It appears that this is a design flaw as there should not be any space that a child could somehow feel safe to stick there legs between a wall and a loft bed. I would also recommend that in the warnings that come with loft beds that they warn parents to make sure bed is flush against the wall or far enough away from the wall that a child may not become entrapped between the wall and the bed. There should also be a warning that placement should not be by a window. Many parents may not think about these things until something tragic like this happens.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a child due to a design flaw in the loft bed, indicating the highest severity level. The likelihood is considered possible as similar incidents could occur with the same design flaw.

incident_description: I received a recall notification from Amazon in regards to a South Shore Libra Collections 3-Drawer Chest purchased on March 14th, 2014.
justification: The description only mentions a recall notification without any incident or injury reported.

incident_description: I purchased a "architect's" clamp-on desk lamp for my mother as a bedside reading lamp.  After one day of use it fell off the headboard and injured her.  I attribute the failure to the plastic clamp.  Other lamps I have of my own have metal clamps.  The plastic clamp flexes slightly but enough to loosen up and slip off the mounting surface.  The rest of the lamp is metal.
justification: The lamp fell and caused an injury due to the plastic clamp's failure, indicating a clear hazard.

incident_description: Our father [REDACTED]  living in assisted living home was suffocated and died as a result of the Drive Medical RTL15063-ADJ Adjustable Height Home Bed Assist Handle which we had purchased for our father.   At 3am on Christmas morning 2016, he became entrapped in the railing system between it and the bed mattress and suffocated.
justification: The incident resulted in death due to suffocation caused by entrapment in the bed railing system.

incident_description: I purchased a Zinus Green Tea mattress from Amazon which I was not aware contained fiberglass until I came across a class action lawsuit. Upon checking my mattress I discovered that the protective cover was faulty and had ripped along the seams about halfway around which Zinus shared could mean that fiberglass would be able to leak. I reached out to customer service and was told that although because the protective cover was ripped it could leak fiberglass, I was required to take off the cover I purchased upon discovering the hazard and take a picture of the mattress being disposed of (exposing myself to the risk of fiberglass) to even begin the process of a requesting a refund. I had already previously sent pictures of the mattress, the default, the tags, and my proof of purchase receipt and discussed the concern of fiberglass exposure which they did not seem to be concerned about.
justification: The incident involves a faulty mattress cover that could leak fiberglass, posing a potential health risk, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description: Purchased a product called Beaverbot which is advertised for being for kids ages 3 and up. I tried it first to see if it was really safe, and there are openings where even an adult can insert their finger and touch moving parts. This is not a product that should be marketed to children if even an adult sized finger can reach dangerous parts. It is also significantly lacking in markings, warnings, and other labels. For example, no warnings about not touching the moving cutting shaft. Also, very limited information about the company itself is available, and their story on the About Us page of their website seems fabricated or AI generated.
justification: The product has design flaws that could lead to injury, especially for children, due to accessible moving parts and lack of warnings.

incident_description: My brother rolled over in the middle of the night and his neck became entangled in the bed rail and he was asphyxiated and he died.
justification: The incident resulted in a death due to asphyxiation from entanglement in the bed rail.

incident_description: A CFL 13w E12 base that was used in our light over our bar in the kitchen caught fire while in use.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
We smelled smoke but could not locate it.  Eventually one of the kids saw the smoke.

The light fixture is marked SUN-LITE and bears a mark "IWI UL 1439" and "Made in China".  The fixture has three glass shades. Each glass shade is held up by no more than a friction fit.  I suspect the friction fit failed, pressing the combustible paper onto the bulb.  The paper then ignited, and later the burning paper dropped to the floor.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a fire hazard but no reported injuries or death.

incident_description: While we slept last night, the television stand for our Samsung PN50C550G1F plasma television exploded, sending glass all over our living room.
justification: The television stand exploded, causing property damage but no reported injuries.

incident_description: Toy literally exploded and caught on fire.
justification: The toy exploding and catching fire poses a significant risk of injury or death.

incident_description:
Invacare manufactures a medical device marketed as a shower chair.

The shower chair has four adjustable legs.  Each leg screws both into and out of the shower chair base, thus allowing the chair to be adjustable to 'fit' individual shower/tub basins.

Each adjustable legs has a designed locking mechanism, unfortunately, in the chair I purchased, lot # XXXXX, the locking mechanism on each of the 4 legs fails to lock the adjustable leg.

A normal customer usage profile shows that the chair will be moved around the shower basin for stuff like cleaning to tub basin, pulling one self into the shower stream, or pushing the chair back to exist the tub basin.

During this normal customer usage profile, the chair legs rotate due to the failure of the leg locking mechanism.  The chair leg rotation causes the legs to randomly adjust, causing the chair to be more and more...."TIPSY" for lack of a better word.

Customers who use this medical device are often disabled, but as often elderly.  Elderly customers often suffer from dementia, altimzers, and the like.  Health care providers who do the initial set up of these medical devices....shower chairs.....are not aware that with each usage by the customer, the care becomes further and further out of level, out of adjustment, and the chair 'TIPSY-NESS' become worse.

As the chair becomes more unstable, the likelihood of a shower slip and fall becomes greater and greater.

You or I can go to [REDACTED] and buy an $8 lawn chair that is waterproof and unadjustable, but will perform the same each and every day in the shower.  An Invacare shower chair is $80 and is more unpredictable each and every day of its use due to leg locking mechanisms that fail to lock the legs in a given spot.
justification: The failure of the locking mechanism leads to an unstable chair, increasing the risk of slips and falls, which could result in injury, especially for elderly or disabled users.

incident_description:
I purchased a large, heavy chandelier from Wayfair in January 2020. The product was installed properly and remained in use without visible issues for several years.

On April 18, 2025, at approximately 7:00 PM, while we were having dinner in the dining room, we suddenly heard a loud crashing sound of glass breaking. Upon inspection, we discovered that the chandeliers main support hook had broken due to the excessive weight of the fixture. As a result, the upper section of the chandelier detached and partially collapsed, causing significant damage to several glass shades and structural components.

Fortunately, because we had installed a secondary safety support during the initial installation, the entire chandelier did not fall completely to the ground. Otherwise, the heavy fixture  weighing several dozen pounds  could have fallen directly onto anyone below, causing serious injury or even death.
justification: The chandelier partially collapsed but no one was injured due to the secondary safety support.

incident_description: LED 4' bulb may have caused several fires in lighting fixtures.
justification: The incident involves potential fires caused by LED bulbs, which could lead to property damage or injury.

incident_description: Purchased the desk in Nov 2012.  The desk has had normal usage since then.  There were no incidents of dropping items on the desk and no visible or known cracks or chips.  Upon entering my office on 4/9/13, I found the desk shattered into hundreds of pieces.
justification: The desk shattered without any prior signs of damage or injury, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
A Cree-type 60watt-equivalent LED light bulb blew apart in an overhead light fixture in my home, with the light switch in the OFF position.  It shattered the fixture's glass protective bowl, spewing glass fragments all over the floor and damaging our laminate flooring.  The bulb itself popped it's glass casing away from the ceramic base, but is pretty much intact.

We're very concerned about the potential for injury to home inhabitants, represented by the possibility of the bulb blowing apart.  It mystifies me why an LED bulb would even blow apart at all when the light switch is Off!  After cleaning up and removing the broken glass and broken light bulb, I personally checked the light fixture and found no flaws. In fact, I screwed in a standard incandescent 60 watt bulb and it functioned perfectly when I turned the light switch to ON.

Home Depot sells these CREE lightbulbs under their house name, but there's no identifying information on the manufacturer. I've written to Home Depot to ask for manufacturer information so i can make a claim for damages.
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injuries, and similar occurrences are rare based on the description.

incident_description:
This letter serves as a formal complaint against Sleep City located at 10140-1 Philips Highway, Jacksonville, Florida 32256 and Sealy Manufacture Company, One Office Parkway @ Sealy Drive, Trinity, North Carolina 27370. At his point, we feel the only thing left for us to do is ask the Consumer Safety Product Commission to investigate Sealy for selling mattresses that pose a health risk because they are designed below the standards. This specific Sealy Mattress we purchased from Sleep City is designed so that the head and feet rest an inch or more lower than the midriff which causes neck and back pain. To see what others customers are saying about Sealy mattresses, please Google Sealy's Consumer Complaints. The following is part of applicable data: Sealy's Queen Mattress, 516126 Queen68660038, PC#2402, PGC#GP02, SN420723122402, Date for Mfg. 07-23-12MJ, and made in Orlando Florida 32837. Despite several pleas to Sealy and Sleep City to send an Inspector out to our home to inspect the Mattress, they have refused to do so. That is because they likely know our complaint is valid.
We would appreciate your agency investigating this product as we firmly believe its construction falls below the standards causing numbness and neck pain. It is time to stop Mattress Companies from selling products that are not structured to provide the comfort and service they claim. We appreciate your service.
justification: The complaint describes neck and back pain from mattress design, indicating injury (severity 3). Occurrence likelihood is possible (3) given multiple customer complaints.

incident_description:

incident_description:

The consumer had came back to the kitchen to find the bulb had popped and the light bulb was hanging from the wires exposed. The consumer's brother in law shut off the power to the fixture and replaced with a common filament light bulb. The consumer is unsure if his bulb is similar to spiral bulbs that have been recalled and is not sure if it has not been recalled. 

The bulb has cinge marks and blackening at the base. The bulb emitted a burning smell of a fire and did not actually see any flames from the light bulb. The consumer decided not to call the fire department at the time of the incident. The bulb is 23 watts, 330AMPS and 120 volts. The light bulb had not flickered just before the incident. The consumer mentioned that he had the bulb in the fixture for 4 months and the bulb was on for 8-10 hours. 

The consumer has yet to call the retailer . The consumer called the firm yesterday and stated that they would call him back and they did not. incident_description:
The mattress has a zipper sewn into the liner.  On the outside of that liner, a tag indicates that it is machine washable.

In early January 2021, the consumer removed the liner and washed it.  However, there is a fiberglass acrylic blanket cover, underneath the mattress.  This cover was used to meet the flammability requirement.

After washing that cover, the fiberglass worked its  way into the mattress, bedding and comforter.  Therefore, airborne fiberglass is all over the place.

The consumer called the manufacturer and sent them an email about this matter.    Initially, the mfrs rep. told them that they were never supposed to remove that part and indicated that this problem was due to customer neglect.

However, after the consumer provided proof of the tag on the mattress.  The firm's rep's started retracting their position and indicated that they had changed the verbiage on their products.

Next, the mfr. indicated that they had done extensive R&D testing.  They also sent the consumer a plastic cover for the mattress, some towels and advised him to wipe everything in the home down thoroughly.

The consumer followed their instructions and washed the items in their home, multiple times, but it did not rectify the matter.

The consumer has a 7 month old in the home and he is concerned for his family.  The manufacturer was still unwilling to do anything further and indicated that they had done their due-diligence.

The consumer called in a remediation company.  They confirmed that there was an extensive amount of fiberglass in the home.

The consumer followed up with the manufacturer again and they responded that they were within compliance relating to the amount of fiberglass within their products.  The mfr.  stopped discussing the aspect that the tag on the mattress indicated that it could be removed and washed.

The consumer has been corresponding with [REDACTED] Mfr's rep.

The consumer's young son has experienced respiratory issues, itchy-red, rash on the skin and coughing and sneezing.

They also contacted the BBB & the state AG Office.
justification: The consumer's young son has experienced respiratory issues, itchy-red rash, and coughing, indicating injury from fiberglass exposure.

incident_description: As part of my duties with the [REDACTED] (a recipient of CDC funding), I performed a child lead poisoning case investigation on 12/29/2022 at the child's home. 12/28/13 The store was contacted and her spouse was informed that the chair set was not under warranty.  He requested that someone came out and look at the product and they informed him that some would be sent out in 1/22/14.  The retailer called back and reschedule visit for 2/17/14.  They came out and informed her that they would repair the chairs but she declined because of the safety hazard.

incident_description: I have owned a kitchen table with a tempered glass top for 2 years, purchased through Wayfair in 2019. Two days ago while we were eating breakfast at the table, the glass spontaneously exploded. There was nothing that prompted this, such as something falling on it. It also did not slowly crack and then break apart; one moment it was a solid table and the next moment it was in a million little pieces. The shattered glass continued to pop on the ground. Aside from glass being everywhere, there were some small pieces that scratched us and some that we had to pull out from between our toes not from walking on it, but just by sitting at it in the moment it exploded. It was just my wife and I, and we have two cats who luckily ran away when they heard the sound. We also have to replace the dishes/glasses that were on top of the table, as well as cases for phones and an [REDACTED] that had small pieces of glass stuck in their cases.
justification: The incident involved spontaneous glass explosion causing minor injuries (scratches and embedded glass pieces) but no severe harm or death.

incident_description:
12/25/2014, 12/26/2014 The consumer's daughter lit her two candles. 

12/27/2014 The consumer's daughter noticed that one of the jars had burnt black, more so than the other one, which appeared to have burned normally. Her daughter told the consumer that her nasal mucus was black. Her daughter did not make the connection that it was possibly due to the candles. 

The consumer's son-in-law was vomiting for a couple of days but the consumer nor her daughter are able to connect his illness to the candles.

01/06/2015 The consumer's daughter lit some candles during dinner, one of which was the second candle in question. 

01/07/2015 The consumer had black nasal mucus as well. When she cleaned her grand child's mucus with cotton swabs, it were also black. The baby nor the consumer took any medications as the consumer decided to let it run its course.

When the consumer went to make the baby a bottle, the white bottle cap was black, as well as all the baby's other bottle caps. Many things in the home were black: bottle caps inside cabinets, utensils, cabinets, toys, portable bath tub, curtains, windows, door corners, chandelier, metal plates for the water sprinkler system that is built into the ceiling, blinds, lighting domes, wood furniture, etc. All in all, most of everything that was plastic or metal on all floor levels. The consumer believes the smoke traveled through the ventilation system, so she decided to change the air filter. The consumer indicates that the filter was completely black.

The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard. The consumer plans on contacting the manufacturer.
justification: The incident caused black nasal mucus and vomiting, indicating minor health effects, but no severe injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
(6/23/2023):  There was an incense stick lit for 2  3 minutes and it was beside the consumers bed.

Embers from a nearby burning incense fell on the bed and caused it to burn.    The consumer laid on the bed afterwards, not knowing embers had gotten on the bed.  He quickly extinguished the burning mattress, but sustained burns to his right wrist.  The consumer mother treated him for 2nd degree burns

Approximately 5 of the mattress was burned.

(7/2023):  The consumer contacted the manufacturer and reported the problem to them.  Initially he was asked if he had a zelle account, which he said yes. The consumer said that the manufacturers rep. agreed to provide a refund, but he never received it. He sent the recall company pictures of his burn, his purchase receipt and other information that they requested.  He called the company a few more times and sent them more emails, but no one responded.

He then contacted the company through Facebook and tried calling the recall number, but no one answer

(2024):  The consumer was notified by the company about CPSC Recall# 24-263.  However, considering his incident, he would like a refund and does not want a replacement mattress cover.
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns to the consumer's wrist, indicating an injury.

incident_description: A electric candle (decrotive the type that is placed on a window sill) Caught my 14 yr old daughter's bed on fire at 2:30 am on 1/02/12.  It had fallen of the window and landed on her bed.  The candle was made by Ting Shen and has the number TS-06 on the plug.  This fixture is UL approved.  UL Sticker have the numbers N-4671 issued N-4671  Also E-1371339.  She was lucky and only had a minor 1st degree burn on her leg.  Her room was filled with smoke as she slept.  The Quilt on her bed has about a 10" Dia. hole burned The rest of the bedding also has holes burned thru  The Mattress has a 4" hole burned into it.
justification: The incident resulted in a first-degree burn and significant property damage, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description:

hazards as noted by numerous complaints.

However, SYLVANIA continues to repond to these safety concerns in a defensive litigious fashion as follows listed in the follwing link.
